Damped oscillator

A five-minute tour

Welcome everyone. Ask who has seen a pendulum slow down.

Equation of motion

$$m\ddot{x} + b\dot{x} + kx = 0$$

Natural frequency \(\omega_0 = \sqrt{k/m}\)

Damping ratio $\zeta = \frac{b}{2\sqrt{mk}}$

Point out that the equation is linear.

Three regimes

Press down for details.

Underdamped

  • $\zeta < 1$: it oscillates
  • The envelope decays as $e^{-\zeta\omega_0 t}$

Critical and overdamped

No oscillation when $\zeta \ge 1$.

Try it

ζ = 0.20

Drag the slider past one and watch the oscillation vanish.

The same in code


function position(t, zeta, omega) {
  return Math.exp(-zeta * omega * t) * Math.cos(omega * Math.sqrt(1 - zeta * zeta) * t);
}
